headline: Committee recommends inclusionary zoning changes for planning review, adding a project size threshold.
summary: Staff would work with the planning board on unit sizes and ratios, income levels, and whether these should vary by zone. The planning board would also look at opportunity zone funding, eliminating the fee in lieu option, and an annual review. The committee also recommended the citizen participation plan for the 2027 to 2031 consolidated plan, which goes to the City Council in December.
decisions: Recommended the citizen participation plan for the 2027 to 2031 consolidated plan to the City Council, 4-0.
Withdrew the motion for a short-term task force on inclusionary zoning.
Approved an amendment adding a project size threshold to the inclusionary zoning changes, 3-0.
Recommended that planning staff work with the planning board to amend the inclusionary zoning ordinance, 3-0.
Referred the fiscal year 2026 tax increment financing annual report to the City Council as a communication item, 4-0.
Referred the annual accomplishments report for the housing and economic development committee to the City Council as a communication item, 4-0.
discussion: Inclusionary zoning changes: Two council proposals gave different unit shares and income levels, including a range of 0 to 10 percent of units and 0 to 150 percent AMI. Members also raised an annual review, applying changes only to future projects, and eliminating the fee in lieu.

Task force versus planning board: Some members asked for a short task force first. Planning staff said the planning board process already includes public workshops and analysis, and that a task force would need a clear charge.

Public speakers on inclusionary zoning: Speakers said the share of approved units that were completed fell from almost 18% to less than 9%, and asked for a lower requirement. Others said the policy should be dropped, or that a three-year review period is too long.

Citizen participation plan: Members asked how the new thresholds would work. Staff said the threshold for a substantial amendment would be $200,000 for CDBG and HOME and $50,000 for ESG, instead of 7% of the annual grant.

Projects already in progress: Members said changes should not reach projects already approved or financed. Staff said the council could add a clause to block changes to approved projects, though an applicant could still reapply under new rules.
